hyperedges.label: AST + Semantic Extraction and Merge Flow

nodes.label: graphify (Vietnamese README)
nodes.rationale: Positioned as the answer to the Karpathy /raw folder problem: 71.5x fewer tokens per query than reading raw files, persistent across sessions.

nodes.label: Three-Pass Pipeline (AST, Whisper, Subagents)
nodes.rationale: Deterministic AST pass extracts code structure without an LLM; only docs, papers, images and transcripts need Claude subagents.

nodes.label: SHA256 Cache
nodes.rationale: Re-runs only process changed files.

nodes.label: Local Processing / No Telemetry
nodes.rationale: Code files are processed locally via tree-sitter AST and video via faster-whisper so content need not leave the machine.

nodes.label: graphify (Simplified Chinese README)
nodes.rationale: Older v3 documentation: two-pass pipeline, pip-only install, no video/audio support.

nodes.label: Two-Pass Pipeline (AST + Claude Subagents)
nodes.rationale: Pass one is deterministic AST analysis requiring no LLM; pass two dispatches Claude subagents in parallel over docs, papers and images.

nodes.label: Leiden Topology Clustering (No Embeddings)
nodes.rationale: Graph structure is itself the similarity signal: Claude-extracted semantically_similar_to edges already live in the graph and influence community partitioning, so no embedding step or vector database is needed.

nodes.label: semantically_similar_to Edge
nodes.rationale: Connects concepts across files that have no structural dependency, e.g. two functions solving the same class of problem without calling each other.

nodes.label: rationale_for Node
nodes.rationale: Docstrings and NOTE/IMPORTANT/HACK/WHY comments are extracted as nodes so the graph records why code was written that way, not only what it does.

nodes.label: confidence_score (0.0-1.0)
nodes.rationale: Every INFERRED edge carries a score so the reader knows not just which edges are guesses but how confident the model is; EXTRACTED edges are always 1.0.

nodes.label: Hyperedges (3+ Node Groups)
nodes.rationale: Expresses group relationships among three or more nodes that pairwise edges cannot represent.

nodes.label: PreToolUse Hook (Ambient Graph Rule)
nodes.rationale: Fires before every Glob and Grep so the assistant reads GRAPH_REPORT.md and navigates by structure instead of grepping the whole project.

nodes.label: AGENTS.md Ambient Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw, Factory Droid and Trae have no PreToolUse hook, so AGENTS.md is their ambient mechanism.

nodes.label: GRAPH_REPORT.md
nodes.rationale: One-page summary of god nodes, community structure and surprising connections, read before searching files.

nodes.label: query / path / explain Commands
nodes.rationale: Traverse graph.json hop by hop to answer a precise question, versus the ambient hook which only gives overall orientation.

nodes.label: --watch Auto-Sync
nodes.rationale: Code saves rebuild instantly via AST with no LLM; doc and image changes only prompt the user to run --update because re-extraction costs tokens.

nodes.label: Git post-commit / post-checkout Hooks
nodes.rationale: Rebuilds the graph after each commit and branch switch without needing a background process.

nodes.label: --wiki Agent-Crawlable Wiki
nodes.rationale: index.md lets any agent navigate the knowledge base through ordinary file reads instead of parsing JSON directly.

nodes.label: 71.5x Token Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Compression grows with corpus size; six files already fit in a context window so the value there is structural clarity rather than token savings.

nodes.label: Tech Stack: NetworkX + Leiden + tree-sitter + vis.js
nodes.rationale: No Neo4j and no server required; the whole system runs locally.

nodes.label: Worked Examples
nodes.rationale: Ships raw inputs alongside real outputs so readers can re-run and verify the numbers themselves — the highest-trust form of contribution.

nodes.label: Three-Stage Pipeline (Traditional Chinese)
nodes.rationale: Deterministic AST traversal extracts code structure without any LLM before transcription and subagent passes run.

nodes.label: Local Whisper / faster-whisper Transcription
nodes.rationale: Video and audio are transcribed locally so media content stays on the machine.

nodes.label: /graphify Command (Kilo)
nodes.rationale: Passes the argument string through unchanged and forbids answering from raw files before handing off, so the skill always owns the response.

nodes.label: graphify Skill (Agents)
nodes.rationale: Any question about a codebase should be treated as a graphify query first when graphify-out/ exists.

nodes.label: Fast Path for Existing Graph
nodes.rationale: If graphify-out/graph.json already exists and the request is a natural-language question rather than a rebuild command, skip Steps 1-5 entirely — the graph is already built, so re-detecting and re-extracting is wasted work.

nodes.label: Step 0 - GitHub Repos and Multi-Path Merge
nodes.rationale: Only runs for URLs or multiple folders; a plain local path skips it.

nodes.label: Step 1 - Interpreter Detection and Install
nodes.rationale: Resolves uv tool, pipx, venv and system installs in order, then writes the interpreter path to .graphify_python so it persists across invocations and every later step uses the same interpreter.

nodes.label: Step 2 - Detect Files
nodes.rationale: Writes the sidecar from Python rather than a shell redirect so the block renders identically on PowerShell hosts without console-encoding drift (#2528); skipped_sensitive files are listed so a wrongly-flagged source is visible and can be renamed (#2106).

nodes.label: Step 2.5 - Video and Audio Transcription
nodes.rationale: Transcripts are treated as doc files in Step 3; skipped entirely when detect returns zero video files.

nodes.label: Step 3 - Extract Entities and Relationships
nodes.rationale: Splits deterministic free structural extraction from token-costing semantic extraction, and runs Part A and Part B in parallel because they operate on different file types — saving 5-15s on large corpora.

nodes.label: No API Key Required Rule
nodes.rationale: Code is extracted structurally with no LLM, and semantic extraction falls back to the host agent itself; graphify never reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY, so prompting for a key is a misread of the skill.

nodes.label: Gemini Semantic Backend
nodes.rationale: Used only if GEMINI_API_KEY or GOOGLE_API_KEY is already set, replacing subagent dispatch; default model gemini-3-flash-preview, overridable via GRAPHIFY_GEMINI_MODEL or --model.

nodes.label: Part A - Structural AST Extraction
nodes.rationale: Deterministic and fast, so it is started while subagents process docs and papers.

nodes.label: .graphify_ast.json
nodes.rationale: Always written, even empty, so Part C's unconditional merge has its input.

nodes.label: Part B - Semantic Extraction via Parallel Subagents
nodes.rationale: The Agent tool is mandatory: reading files one-by-one is 5-10x slower. A code-only corpus still writes an empty semantic file, because Part C reads .graphify_semantic.json unconditionally and would otherwise hit FileNotFoundError.

nodes.label: Step B0 - Semantic Cache Check
nodes.rationale: Cache entries are attributed to the extraction prompt file so an upgraded prompt forces re-extraction while an unchanged one replays entries (#1939). Only content files (document, paper, image) are checked — flattening every category makes subagents re-read code already covered by AST (#1392).

nodes.label: .graphify_cached.json
nodes.rationale: Deleted when there are no cache hits so Part C never merges a stale file from a prior run (#1392).

nodes.label: Step B1 - Split Into Chunks
nodes.rationale: Each image gets its own chunk because vision needs separate context; same-directory files are grouped so cross-file relationships are more likely to be extracted.

nodes.label: Step B2 - Dispatch All Subagents in One Message
nodes.rationale: All Task calls go in the same response so they run in parallel.

nodes.label: references/extraction-spec.md
nodes.rationale: Loaded only when at least one chunk holds a doc, paper or image; a pure-code corpus skips Part B and never reads it.

nodes.label: .graphify_chunk_NN.json
nodes.rationale: Existence on disk is the success signal for a subagent; an absolute CHUNK_PATH derived from cwd is required because Part C globs graphify-out/ relative to the project root, not the scan dir (#1392).

nodes.label: Step B3 - Collect, Cache, and Merge
nodes.rationale: A missing chunk file means the subagent was likely dispatched read-only, so it warns rather than silently skipping; real token counts are read from the Agent result usage field because chunk JSON always carries placeholder zeros. The same SPEC_PATH as Step B0 must be passed, or a write under a different prompt lands where the next read won't look (#1939).

nodes.label: Part C - Merge AST + Semantic
nodes.rationale: AST nodes go first and semantic nodes are deduplicated by id.

nodes.label: Step 4 - Build, Cluster, Analyze, Generate
nodes.rationale: root= mirrors the --update runbook so full builds and incremental updates never drift apart on re-extract (#1361).

nodes.label: Empty-Graph Guard
nodes.rationale: Checked immediately after build and before any write so an empty extraction cannot clobber a good graph.json, GRAPH_REPORT.md or analysis sidecar (#1392).

nodes.label: Shrink Guard (#479)
nodes.rationale: to_json writes nothing and returns False when the new graph is smaller than the existing graph.json; the report and analysis sidecar are only written when the graph actually landed, so they never describe a graph graph.json doesn't contain (#1392).

nodes.label: --directed Flag / IS_DIRECTED Substitution
nodes.rationale: Builds a DiGraph preserving edge direction source→target; default is an undirected Graph.

nodes.label: Step 4.5 - Graph Health Check
nodes.rationale: Read-only and never aborts, because the graph is still usable — but edge collapse, dangling/missing endpoints and self-loops are the silent-corruption modes of incremental updates and AST/LLM id mismatches, so the warning must be surfaced per the Honesty Rules.

nodes.label: Step 5 - Label Communities
nodes.rationale: Questions are regenerated with real labels because labels affect question phrasing, and graph.json is re-exported so nodes carry the curated community_name (#2490).

nodes.label: Step 6 - Obsidian Vault + HTML Export
nodes.rationale: HTML is always generated unless --no-viz; the Obsidian vault is opt-in because it generates one file per node. HTML auto-aggregates to a community view above 5000 nodes.

nodes.label: Steps 6b-8 - Flag-Gated Exports
nodes.rationale: Run only on their flags; the token benchmark runs when total_words exceeds 5,000. --wiki must run before Step 9 cleanup so .graphify_labels.json still exists.

nodes.label: Semantic Manifest Stamping
nodes.rationale: Only semantic files that actually produced output are stamped: a detected file whose chunk failed must stay unstamped so the next --update re-queues it, otherwise it is marked done and its content is lost forever (#2015). Dispatched-but-unstamped files have their stale semantic_hash cleared so detect_incremental re-queues them (#1948). scan_corpus uses the raw full corpus so newly-excluded files are dropped rather than masquerading as deletions (#1908). Manifest keys are relativized to the scan root for portability across clones (#1417). Code files are always stamped because AST is deterministic.

nodes.label: Guide-After-Pipeline Behaviour
nodes.rationale: Only God Nodes, Surprising Connections and Suggested Questions are pasted, then the most boundary-crossing question is offered — each answer ends with a follow-up so the session feels like navigation rather than a one-shot report. The graph is the map; the agent is the guide.
